attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as an inter-VLAN router between node2 and node3, which each sit in their own subnet behind it. node1's eth1 (192.168.10.1/24) faces node2's enp8s0 (192.168.10.2/24, VLAN A) and eth2 (192.168.20.1/24) faces node3's enp8s0 (192.168.20.2/24, VLAN B). IPv4 forwarding was enabled globally and per-interface on node1, and static cross-VLAN routes were added on node2/node3 via NetworkManager (persistent). node2 and node3 now ping each other across the VLAN boundary via node1 (confirmed by ttl=63, one router hop). All config was made persistent: node1 via a custom systemd oneshot service ([REDACTED].service) that reapplies interface IPs/forwarding after the native SONiC interfaces-config/networking services run, and node2/node3 via NetworkManager connection profiles. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (native `reboot`), each polled back to availability with a changed boot_id proving an actual restart (not just a service bounce), and post-restart checks confirmed the routed interfaces, forwarding sysctls, static routes, and end-to-end cross-VLAN ping all recovered automatically without any manual reconfiguration.
